title: Pattern scope and text block indentation

questions.stem: Per this page, in `if (!(obj instanceof Double d)) { A } else { B }`, where can the code use `d`?

options.text: In A only, where the negated test came out true
options.says: In A the match failed, so obj is not a Double there; the page says the variable is available in the else branch of a negated condition.

options.text: In B only, where the match is known to have held
options.says: The page says the variable is in scope only where the compiler can prove the match succeeded, which for a negated condition is the else branch.

options.text: In both A and B, as d is declared in the condition
options.says: The page says the variable is in scope only where the match is proven to have succeeded, not everywhere after its declaration.

origin.section: Q3: How does pattern matching for instanceof work, and what are its scope rules?

questions.stem: Per this page, a text block's content lines are indented 8 spaces and its closing `"""` is indented 12. How much indentation do the result's lines keep?

options.text: None, since 8 is the smallest indent among those lines
options.says: The page strips the minimum leading whitespace across the content lines and the closing line, here 8, and says a delimiter further right does not add indentation.

options.text: All 8, since only a delimiter further left strips it
options.says: The page's algorithm strips the minimum indentation of the content and closing lines in every case; here that minimum is the content's 8 spaces.

options.text: Four, the gap between the content and the delimiter
options.says: The page says a closing delimiter further right does not add indentation, because the minimum rule decides what is stripped.

origin.section: Q2: Explain incidental whitespace stripping in text blocks.
